thread.title_full: Mexico World Cup hero given one last shot at glory with tearful farewell appearance - NewsBreak

author: Joseph McBride
title: Mexico World Cup hero given one last shot at glory with tearful farewell appearance - NewsBreak
text:
By Joseph McBride ,
45 minutes ago Legendary World Cup goalkeeper Guillermo Ochoa said farewell to the Estadio Azteca, currently known as Mexico City Stadium, after making an emotional entrance during a 3-0 win over Czechia.
Ochoa has announced he intends to retire after his sixth World Cup , making him the only other player not named Lionel Messi or Cristiano Ronaldo to make six World Cup rosters. Mexico swept its World Cup group without conceding a goal, becoming the first team to do so since 1990.
Mexico is one of three host nations at this World Cup , and has also been the unexpected base of the Iranian national team following complications with the U.S . But during a historic night for Mexico, Ochoa made his grand entrance and waved goodbye to his professional soccer career in style.

• USA World Cup hero faces wild political attack over 'transplanting Sharia Law'
It was heavily speculated that Ochoa would start Wednesday's game against Czechia, but he was named on the bench as the in-form Raul Rangel was selected. However, as Mexico led 2-0 following goals from Julian Quinones and Mateo Chavez, Ochoa began warming up and was brought on.
The Mexico City crowd went crazy for Ochoa, who clapped the fans as he ran onto the field. It was the perfect cameo for Ochoa as he kept a clean sheet, and Alvaro Fidalgo grabbed a third for Mexico.
After the full-time whistle was blown, Ochoa was swarmed by his teammates and lifted up while being tossed in the air. He was then seen kissing the goalposts at the Azteca as he left the field for possibly the final time.
Ochoa will turn 41 after the World Cup and retire as a global legend of the game. Ochoa has enjoyed a memorable career across Mexico and Europe, but is best known for his international appearances.
He first made the World Cup roster in 2006, but was the third-choice goalkeeper in Germany. The following year, Ochoa was promoted to backup goalkeeper and began earning appearances in the Gold Cup and Copa América.
Ochoa then became Mexico's primary goalkeeper during qualifying for the 2010 World Cup in South Africa, and was named in the Team of the Tournament after the national team won the 2009 Gold Cup. Controversially, he was demoted to backup for the World Cup.
His World Cup debut finally came in 2014, arguably his most memorable summer with Mexico. Ochoa kept a clean sheet in a 1-0 win over Cameroon, and then was named Player of the Match for making four huge saves in a 0-0 draw against host nation Brazil.
"It was the match of my life," Ochoa said at the time. "To do it in a World Cup, in front of all the fans, it's incredible."
Mexico then advanced to the knockout rounds, and Ochoa starred during a 2-1 defeat to the Netherlands. Ochoa kept Mexico ahead as they nursed a 1-0 lead, but the Netherlands eventually came back, scoring the winner from the penalty spot in the 91st minute.
In 2018, Ochoa made nine saves during a 1-0 win over Germany and a total of 25 saves across Mexico's four games. In 2022, Ochoa saved a Robert Lewandowski penalty as Mexico drew 0-0 in the group opener against Poland, but that was his final appearance in Qatar.
summary: 33 minutes ago Legendary World Cup goalkeeper Guillermo Ochoa said farewell to the Estadio Azteca, currently known as Mexico City Stadium, after making an emotional entrance during a 3-0 win over Czechia. But during a historic night for Mexico, Ochoa made his grand entrance and waved goodbye to his professional soccer career in style.
